economy.summary: Wrote in June 2026 that Pennsylvania should reverse its decision to decouple from the federal tax law's business expensing provisions, calling expensing the greatest stimulator of economic growth in the new tax law and saying the decoupling imposes higher taxes on job-creating investment.
economy.short: Urges restoring conformity with federal business expensing rules.

taxes.summary: In a July 2026 statement on the state budget, said spending remains too high and the structural deficit remains around $5 billion, and criticized the budget's use of an accounting maneuver to defer $1.2 billion in payments to the next year; he has also introduced House Bill 1703, which would raise the state and local tax deduction cap for owners of pass-through businesses.
taxes.short: Says spending too high; criticizes deficit; proposes business deduction bill.

abortion.summary: Voted in July 2022 for Senate Bill 106, a proposed state constitutional amendment providing that there is no constitutional right to taxpayer-funded abortion or any other right relating to abortion, and co-sponsored House Bill 2252, a proposed amendment providing that there is no right to abortion or funding for an abortion.
abortion.short: Voted for amendment stating no constitutional right to abortion.

education.summary: Co-sponsors legislation by Rep. Tom Jones that would keep state payments to school districts and social service agencies flowing at the previous year's levels for recurring items when a state budget is not passed by July 1; Greiner said the proposal offers a safety net for school districts, which must pass their own budgets by that date.
education.short: Co-sponsors bill continuing school payments when state budget is late.

energy.summary: Is the author of a 2025 co-sponsorship memo for legislation that would require electric and natural gas suppliers to print contract start and end dates in clear and conspicuous language on customer bills and to notify customers placed on default service, saying it would protect consumers from rate shock when a supply contract lapses.
energy.short: Proposes requiring energy suppliers to print contract dates on bills.

guns.summary: Co-sponsored House Bill 659 in 2021, legislation that would have repealed the requirement to obtain a license to carry a concealed firearm in Pennsylvania.
guns.short: Co-sponsored bill repealing concealed-carry license requirement.

economy.summary: Names cost of living as the most pressing issue facing the district, saying he would work to slow rising rent and mortgage prices and would focus on local business and attractions to bring more employment and money into the district from outside.
economy.short: Names cost of living top issue; would slow rent, mortgage increases.

taxes.summary: Says no single change would streamline the state budget process because the budget is large and has many parts, but suggests starting work on it sooner and keeping members from leaving the Capitol or taking extended breaks until it is passed could encourage a faster process.
taxes.short: Proposes starting budget work sooner, keeping members at Capitol until passage.

energy.summary: Supports state legislative oversight of data center development, saying that history shows local areas have been negatively impacted when large corporations come in and use natural resources freely.
energy.short: Supports state legislative oversight of data centers' natural resource use.
